purpose: Clean reviewer-input benchmark for testing whether an LLM moves from a visible local hashing symptom to the deepest evidence-supported compatibility/coupling boundary and a falsifiable root-complete repair direction without seeing evaluator expectations.

scenario.product: A maintained WordPress integration plugin adds presentation behavior on top of Gravity Flow.

upstream.name: Gravity Flow
properties: implementation not controlled by the integration plugin
comment, whitespace, and internal source reshaping may occur without changing the behavior the integration actually needs

implementation_decisions: use a Gravity Flow internal seam
admit the host only when an exact supported version matches
hash several upstream internal files and require exact fingerprints before the presentation capability is admitted
fail closed for unknown host implementations
treat a fingerprint mismatch as compatibility failure even when the required host behavior has not been shown to differ

two prior admission failures occurred on different fingerprinted files after non-behavioral upstream source changes; bounded runtime probes still showed the presentation behavior required by the integration
no inspected evidence in this scenario establishes that a safer supported public hook/API, capability probe, or stable behavioral seam is available
scenario.local_performance_detail: the same upstream files are hashed repeatedly across requests, making hash caching an obvious local optimization

review_task: Review the engineering decision at causal depth. Identify the local symptom, synthesize the separate fingerprint-mismatch manifestations when evidence supports one failure class, identify the exact-version/internal-source coupling and independently evolving lifecycle property, and seek the deepest evidence-supported causal boundary while preserving what remains NOT_PROVEN. Reject a local hash-cache optimization as defect-class closure if the same coupling survives elsewhere. Compare only materially distinct evidence-supported root-correct directions at the same abstraction level; do not invent a supported seam. State whether repair selection is ready or verification is required, and define success/falsification criteria that would distinguish a root-complete repair from a superficially passing surface patch.
